sources: Defence Minister Israel Katz, on-record remarks at a ceremony, via AFP
fault_line: Katz says no withdrawal from Gaza, Lebanon or Syria -- ever. Eisenkot is reportedly planning the opposite. Which Israel is real: the caretaker that won't leave, or the incoming government that might?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- Katz said it] Katz said: 'With regard to Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons -- alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger.' He also said: 'We will not withdraw from the security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and if the terrorist organisation Hezbollah chooses to join Iran in an attack on Israel, it will suffer extremely severe blows.' [ALLEGATION -- the nuclear-weapons charge] Katz renewed the charge that Iran is pursuing nuclear weapons, which Tehran denies; no IAEA finding is cited in-window. NDTV/AFP note Netanyahu 'has repeatedly threatened new strikes against Iran in recent weeks.'
sections.what_verified: 1 tiered family carrying the actor's own statement: AFP (T1). Straits Times (T3), Arab News (T3), NDTV (T3) and FMT all carry the same AFP dispatch, so they are one family, not four. Gulf News and Khaleej Times liveblogs also carry AFP.
sections.what_disputed: Katz speaks for the outgoing Netanyahu government, not for Eisenkot: Eisenkot's camp has neither confirmed nor denied the Kol Hai report. IAEA has published no new finding in-window supporting the renewed nuclear-weapons charge; Iran denies pursuing nuclear weapons. Katz's June 2026 line ('Israel will not withdraw from Lebanon, even if the Americans demand it') is the standing policy of the outgoing government, not necessarily of the next one.
sections.why_matters: Hours after Eisenkot was tipped to pull out of Lebanon, the sitting defence minister said the opposite: nobody is withdrawing from anywhere -- and the Iran mission 'is still not complete.'
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (first surfaced Gulf News liveblog 13:51 , in the 1300-1400 window, missed by the 1400 scan; in-window corroboration EconoTimes 11:22Z = 15:22 ; FMT 19:00 MYT = 15:00 ) -- Defence Minister Katz: 'mission not complete' on Iran; Israel will NOT withdraw from security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria

totw_analysis: Our read: Hours after Eisenkot was tipped to pull out of Lebanon, the sitting defence minister said the opposite: nobody is withdrawing from anywhere -- and the Iran mission 'is still not complete.' The fault line our audience is arguing over: Katz says no withdrawal from Gaza, Lebanon or Syria -- ever. Eisenkot is reportedly planning the opposite. Which Israel is real: the caretaker that won't leave, or the incoming government that might?
